Greetings, everyone!
Welcome to the 2026 VSiN College Football Betting Guide! This is the most important Guide 
that we put out because it is so hard to follow the college football offseason and we have 
previews for all 138 FBS teams to help you prepare for the season ahead.
To say that this is a team effort is an understatement, so before I explain more about what’s in 
this year’s edition, I’d like to thank Senior Editor Zachary Cohen, Editor Michael Dolan, Guide 
Designer Matt Devine, and everybody on our creative and marketing teams. We also had a 
ton of host participation in terms of best bets and heartfelt thanks go out to all of those who 
submitted picks and predictions.
Special thanks to these fantastic writers for the best preseason content you are going to find 
anywhere:

And, of course, our VSiN Analytics Guru Steve Makinen, who has provided his Favorite Season 
Win Total Bets, Power Ratings Projections, and Stats and Ratings for all of the teams.
You can find VSiN on SiriusXM Channel 158, on the VSiN Watch App, on YouTube TV as part

DAVE ROSS
VIRGINIA TECH OVER 6.5 WINS (-140) &
ALT OVER 7.5 WINS (+120
I’m going with the silver-bullet approach: one shot. Firing on 
all Virginia Tech futures. Over 6.5 at -140 and adjusted Over 7.5 
at +120.
I love their chances this year to really compete in year one 
under James Franklin. The funny thing is, he was in the CFP 
semis two years ago and then ran out of Happy Valley for 
Blacksburg. One man’s trash is another man’s treasure. He’ll 
thrive in Hokieland, and keeping Brent Pry as the DC is the 
hidden gem. One of the best, if not the biggest, winners in the 
portal. Don’t be surprised if they find themselves in Charlotte 
playing for an ACC title this year. I won’t be.
MATT YOUMANS
FRESNO STATE OVER 6.5 WINS (-120)
Matt Entz coached North Dakota State to two FCS national 
championships in five years and compiled a 60-11 record. Last 
year, he took over a losing Fresno team and produced a 9-4 
finish. That team was limited by mediocre quarterback play, 
and Entz brought in Maryland transfer Khristian Martin, a 
dual-threat playmaker. Four of the top five pass catchers are 
returning, including leading receiver Josiah Freeman. Three 
of the top offensive linemen in the Pac-12 pave the way for 
experienced running backs Bryson Donelson and Rayshon 
Luke. The Bulldogs host Boise State on Oct. 10 in what could 
be the most important matchup of Pac-12 play. Entz coached 
Fresno, a 17-point underdog, to a 30-7 win at Boise last year. 
After a trip to USC in early September, Fresno has a realistic 
shot to reel off three consecutive wins against Sacramento State, 
San Jose State and Rice. Circa Sports posted 6.5 with the league’s 
12th flex game included in the win total.
MICHIGAN UNDER 8.5 WINS (-160)
The Big Ten is loaded again this season — starting with 
Ohio State, Oregon and Indiana — and the Wolverines have 
been losing ground. The fallout from the Jim Harbaugh era 
ended with the firing of Sherrone Moore, who led a clumsy 
coaching staff that failed to develop freshman quarterback 
Bryce Underwood. The talent level is down and the schedule’s 
degree of difficulty is up. Michigan will play the Buckeyes and 
Ducks on the road and host Indiana, Iowa, Penn State and 
Oklahoma. The hiring of veteran coach Kyle Whittingham is 
a huge positive, but almost everything would need to go right 
for the Wolverines to win nine games, and it’s more likely 
Whittingham will go 7-5. The price is getting high (-160 or 
more), but pay it.
DAVE TULEY
TEXAS TO WIN SEC (+295) &
NATIONAL CHAMPIONSHIP (+700)
Longtime readers of my Tuley’s Takes columns, especially in 
horse racing, know I am not deterred when a bet on a team 
(or horse) comes up short, as I’d rather be too early on a team/
horse peaking than too late. Last year, I bet Texas to win the 
CFB Playoff and obviously came up short as QB Arch Manning 
didn’t reach his well-bred potential as early as I was hoping, 
The Longhorns had a disappointing season but showed signs 
of competence, and I’m hoping that I was just a year too early 
(similar to me betting the Detroit Lions to win this season’s 
Super Bowl after losing with them last year). Texas is the 
second-betting choice in the SEC behind Georgia, and obviously 
we’re hoping they win the conference on the way to the CFB 
Playoff and natty.


===== [PAGE 6] =====
6
2026 VSiN COLLEGE FOOTBALL BETTING GUIDE
INDIANA TO WIN BIG TEN (+245)
Also last year, I wasn’t a believer in Indiana for most of the season, but 
fortunately grabbed the Hoosiers at +330 to win the College Football 
Playoff in the VSiN Bowl Betting Guide and rode them to the title. 
Obviously they lost Heisman Trophy winner Fernando Mendoza as the 
NFL’s No. 1 overall draft pick, but coach Curt Cignetti has to be given his 
due for one of the biggest turnarounds in not only CFB but sports history 
with the Indiana football program, and I’m confident he’ll have them in 
the running again. It looks like a three-horse race in the Big Ten between 
Indiana, Ohio State and Oregon, so +245 is a fair price. And I might also 
take a shot at the Hoosiers to repeat as national champions, as it feels 
like they’re being overlooked at just short of 13-1.
TOLEDO TO WIN MAC (+365)
As an alumnus of Northern Illinois (class of 1988), I’ve been a longtime 
fan of the Mid-American Conference. I have mixed feelings about the 
Huskies moving to the Mountain West Conference this season, as I’ll be 
able to go to their games at UNLV every other year but will miss watching 
them in the MAC. But I’m still a MAC fan and see this as another three-
horse race with Toledo, Western Michigan and Miami-Ohio. Toledo has a 
new coach in Mike Jacobs, who has won everywhere he’s been, including 
two straight SoCon titles at Mercer. And Toledo is used to rebuilding 
after losing coaches, as happens with mid-majors, and competing every 
year. Running back CJ Miller and WR Adjatay Dabbs come from Mercer 
with Jacobs to help whoever wins the QB job.
AARON MOORE
TEXAS TO WIN NATIONAL CHAMPIONSHIP (+700) 
Sign me up as a follower of the Arch Manning Redemption Tour. The 
prized QB at the start of last season was far from being someone who 
could lead his team to a national championship. The version at the tail 
end of last year was a lot closer to doing so. Besides more experience for 
Manning and leading WR Ryan Wingo, Texas added another downfield 
threat with Auburn transfer Cam Coleman. The offense will be there, 
and Will Muschamp on the sidelines should help the defense. After the 
Big Ten flexed its muscles with a national championship the past three 
seasons, the 7-1 on the Longhorns is a good buy-low scenario for what 
should be one of the two best teams in the SEC.
CLEMSON UNDER 5.5 CONFERENCE WINS (-150)
The ACC schedule makers didn’t do Dabo Swinney any favors as he looks 
to lift the Tigers back into contention. Sure, Clemson is warming up to 
the transfer portal, but the odd migration patterns of the ACC will make it 
hard for Clemson to secure six conference wins. A mid-September flight to 
Berkeley comes in between home games against North Carolina and Miami. 
The end of their season features three of their last four games on the road.
SMU TO REACH ACC CHAMPIONSHIP GAME (+200) 
If veteran QB Kevin Jennings can lead his team to at least one win during 
SMU’s first two conference games of the season (at Florida State and at 
Louisville), the Mustangs will be set up nicely for the remainder of ACC 
play. There should be plenty of October and November ACC wins for the 
Mustangs. The finale in Palo Alto comes on the heels of a trip to South 
Bend, but it is hard now to envision Stanford being a roadblock to a 
championship game appearance.
STEVE MAKINEN
TEXAS TO MAKE COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF (-200) 
Over the last two springs, the Texas staff has brought in the No. 1 and 
No. 3 ranked recruit/transfer classes in the country according to 247 
Sports. To me, that means this locker room is probably the most talented 
in the country this season. Now naturally, that talent has to be cultured 
on the field, but head coach Steve Sarkisian has proven he can do that, 
taking the Longhorns to the CFP title game two years ago. Last year, to 
me, was an unrealistic set of expectations for this team, as the pressure 
on Texas and QB Arch Manning was palpable every time they took the 
field. The fact that the Longhorns still won 10 games despite a 5-7-1 ATS 
record shows just how much even the experts behind the bookmaking 
counter thought of this group. This team won its final three games of ’25 
after some of that pressure was lifted, and Manning exploded in those 
contests. The offense put up 456 yards in the bowl win over Michigan. 
That is the momentum they will be carrying into 2026. The fact that this 
program plays the toughest schedule in the nation this year, according 
to my numbers, is relevant to a degree, but in my opinion, it is Texas’ 
opponents who are drawing the short straw here. I don’t see a team with 
this much talent losing more than a couple of games, in which case a 
playoff berth will be a lock.
 
BOISE STATE TO MAKE COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF (+450)
Last year, two Group of Five teams made the CFP despite losing game(s) 
in the regular season. This year, I expect that total to be one. To me, 
the most likely candidate is Boise State, which moves over to the newly 
formed Pac-12. When I ran my updated power ratings versus the 2026 
schedule, the Broncos’ +1.7 difference was one of the biggest I’ve ever 
had. I think the oddsmakers are giving a bit too much credit to the 
strength of the new conference, where BSU is the clear favorite. QB 
Maddux Madsen returns as a senior, and HC Spencer Danielson is in his 
fourth year with the program. The opener at Oregon is the only likely 
loss I see on the ’26 slate. By the time it’s all said and done in December, 
I believe this team will have the strongest resume of the non-P4 teams.
UNLV TO MAKE MOUNTAIN WEST CONFERENCE TITLE GAME (+110)
I have gone through the UNLV schedule for ’26, which is minus nemesis 
Boise State this year after the Broncos left for the Pac-12, and I am 
struggling to find even a single game where the Runnin’ Rebels will not be 
expected to win or at least be extremely competitive. With the meteoric rise 
New Mexico made last year, the Runnin’ Rebels’ Mountain West consistency 
in recent years makes them the favorite in the MWC this season. Including 
Auburn transfer QB Jackson Arnold, UNLV head coach Dan Mullen has 
brought in highly respected recruiting classes to carry on the momentum of 
30-12 over the past three years. Mullen has been able to bring in numerous 
P4 transfers, which should have the Runnin’ Rebels in the hunt for MWC 
titles year in and year out for the near future. Running this team’s power 
rating against the 2026 schedule produced a 9-3 record, 6.2-1.8 in league 
play. I think +110 to reach the MWC title game is a gift of a line.
TYLER SHOEMAKER
ARKANSAS UNDER 4.5 WINS (-170) 
TSI projects just 4.3 wins for the Razorbacks this year, but when you 
comb through the schedule and look at the win probabilities in a 
vacuum, there are only two games in which they have a > 60% win 
probability, but 10 (!) games in which the win probability is < 40%, with 
zero games falling in the middle as “coin flips.” So, it’s going to take them 
way overachieving relative to expectation in three games, plus winning 
the two they’re supposed to, in order for this bet to lose.
SOUTHERN MISS UNDER 3.5 WINS (+105)

LSU OVER 8.5 WINS (-104 - 3 UNITS) &
TO MAKE COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF (+240) 
The Tigers have some very tough games on the schedule, but they’ll play

there’s a decent chance they go 3-1 in those contests. LSU will no longer

This is going to be a very well-coached team, and the talent is undeniable.

MICHIGAN OVER 8.5 WINS (+140 - 1.5 UNITS) 
Michigan has home games against Oklahoma, Iowa, Penn State, and

from Utah.
This team is big, physical, and talented, so nine wins should be 
expected, even with things in Ann Arbor having taken a strange turn 
since the 2023 championship.
WISCONSIN OVER 6.5 WINS (+100 - 3 UNITS) &
ALT OVER 7.5 WINS (+230) 
This is undoubtedly a bit of a homer pick, and it’s one I believe I’ve lost 
every year since I started working for VSiN. However, this is where we 
list the futures we have for the upcoming college football season, and 
these are two of mine.
Things have been miserable since Luke Fickell took over the Wisconsin 
program, but they were trending in the wrong direction long before he 
was hired. The Badgers were getting smoked by the Big Ten’s elite teams, 
and the program’s recruiting was in the toilet. Fickell has at least turned 
around the latter, which is part of the reason why the 2026 team is as

should help address the team’s competitiveness when facing superior 
programs.
This year, Wisconsin doesn’t play many of the big brands. The 
toughest games on the schedule feature the Badgers facing Notre 
Dame (in Green Bay), Penn State (road), USC (home), and Iowa

daunting matchups.
The reality is that Fickell has been just as unlucky as he has been bad. 
His quarterback rooms have been decimated by injuries since he 
arrived in Madison. If the team can keep Old Dominion transfer Colton 
Joseph healthy, the Badgers will have a dynamic dual-threat playmaker 
under center. They’ll also have a much-improved offensive line, and the 
defense is absolutely loaded — with Fickell having done great work to 
keep Mason Posa and Cooper Catalano around.
Things should start trending in the right direction for Wisconsin this 
year, and eight wins should be the goal.

NEW MEXICO TO WIN THE MOUNTAIN WEST (+265)
If you don’t know the name Jason Eck by now, you will soon.

UCLA OVER 6.5 WINS (+110)
If there are 1,000 Bob Chesney believers, I am one. If there are 100

at every level of college football, in Westwood from the very start. 
Everybody in CFB is clamoring for the next Curt Cignetti. To me,

teams with a win total of 5.5 or lower.
KENTUCKY OVER 4.5 WINS (-148)

DUSTIN SWEDELSON
DARIAN MENSAH TO WIN THE HEISMAN TROPHY (16-1)
We have reached a point in the new landscape of college football where 
we know which programs handle the transfer portal best. Maybe no 
team has been better at finding QBs in the portal and maximizing 
their abilities than the Miami Hurricanes. When Cam Ward arrived 
in Coral Gables two seasons ago, he had averaged 3,484 passing yards 
and 24 passing touchdowns at Washington State over two seasons. He 
then transformed into a Heisman Trophy finalist and eventual No. 1 
overall draft pick by throwing for over 4,300 yards and 39 touchdowns. 
In 2025, Carson Beck transferred from Georgia. Beck finished 
with a career high 30 touchdowns and led Miami to the National 
Championship Game. Now enters Darian Mensah, fresh off 3,900-plus 
passing yards and 34 touchdowns, while leading Duke to the 2025 ACC 
Championship. If he gets the bump that his predecessors received 
in their one year playing in offensive coordinator Shannon Dawson’s 
offense, then he will be in New York for the Heisman ceremony at 
the end of the year. How does he get there aside from scheme? Well, 
throwing to sophomore superstar WR Malachi Toney certainly helps. 
Toney led the nation in receptions and the ACC in receiving yards 
and receiving touchdowns last year. He is capable of taking short 
passes a long way, which will not only boost Mensah’s stats but also 
open up opportunities for others in the offense. That’s where Cooper 
Barkate comes in. Barkate was with Mensah at Duke last season after 
previously playing at Harvard. He quickly became Mensah’s go-to 
target, finishing with 72 catches, 1,106 yards and seven TDs. They 
already have chemistry and, combined with Toney, could form the best 
QB-plus-two-WR combination in the nation. The Hurricanes also added 
WR transfer Cam Vaughn, who had 800 yards and five TDs two seasons 
ago at Jacksonville State, and former South Carolina WR Vandrevius 
Jacobs, who was productive with 548 yards and four touchdowns a 
season ago. Factor in the Miami defense lost some major pieces to the 
NFL, which could result in more shootouts and gaudy stats for Mensah. 
This number is also just too long for the QB of the largest favorite to 
win a Power Four league.
KENTUCKY OVER 4.5 WINS (-150)
There is a lot to like here, even with the challenges of Kentucky being 
a basketball school. The Wildcats scored 17 points or fewer six times in 
2025 and still found five wins on the schedule. If the offense can improve 
a little, they should be able to at least maintain five wins and get over 
this total. That’s why they turned to Will Stein. While Stein has never 
been a head coach before, he did guide an Oregon offense the last three 
seasons that turned Bo Nix into a first-round pick, Dillon Gabriel into a 
third-round pick, and took Dante Moore from UCLA cast-off to potential 
top-five draft pick. His latest QB project is Kenny Minchey. Minchey 
didn’t see a lot of action at Notre Dame, but he battled current Heisman 
Trophy favorite CJ Carr down the stretch for the starting job a year ago. 
Multiple beat reporters appeared on VSiN and thought Minchey had the 
clear leg up in the competition. Whether those practices in South Bend, 
Indiana, translate to game results in Lexington, Kentucky, remains to be 
seen, but it does let us know the talent the Wildcats have under center 
this year. Stein is making sure he has big targets to throw to, bringing 
in big-body transfers at WR. LSU transfer Nic Anderson (6’4”, 205 lbs.) 
had almost 800 yards and 10 TDs at Oklahoma in 2023, Southern Utah 
transfer Shane Carr (6’2”, 185 lbs.) went for over 1,300 yards and 10 TDs 
over the last two seasons, plus Arkansas transfer Ja’Kayden Ferguson 
(6’2”, 184 lbs.) and UAB transfer Xavier Daisy (6’3”, 212 lbs.) join the fold 
as well. The run game gets a huge upside boost from former Texas RB 
CJ Baxter, who missed all of 2024 with an injury. And most importantly, 
they rebuilt this offensive line with four-star transfers in Tennessee OT 
Lance Heard, Ohio State OG Tegra Tshabola, and Baylor center Coleton 
Price. The defense brings in plenty of talent from all over, but the reason 
I bet this is the improved offense. If they reach their potential, they 
could even get to six wins this year.
NC STATE OVER 7.5 WINS (+105)
Dave Doeren enters Year 16 at NC State, where he has only failed to get 
to eight wins one time since 2020. It may not be pretty, and it may not 
excite you, but Doeren wins football games. The offense that scored 30.2 
points per game a year ago lost some juice with Hollywood Smothers 
and its five leading pass catchers leaving. But QB CJ Bailey returns for 
his third season and his second under offensive coordinator Kurt Roper. 
It’s shocking Bailey stayed in Raleigh; he could have made a lot of money 
in the portal after throwing for 3,105 yards, 31 total TDs and nine INTs. 
His return is why this team can get to eight wins. He is a special player 
and should have some help via the transfer portal. WR Davion Dozier 
comes in from App State, where he had 448 yards and five TDs in eight 
games last year. The Wolfpack also added two underutilized Miami WR 
transfers in JoJo Trader and Chance Robinson. While 5’8” Victor Snow 
might be the most interesting, as he is coming off 815 yards and eight 
TDs at Buffalo. LT Jimarion McCrimon, who joins from East Carolina, 
was a massive addition. But most notably, the defense, which allowed 
the second-most explosive plays in the ACC, has been upgraded with 
five potential starters. Edge Harvey Dyson led the American with eight 
sacks a year ago. LBs Raul Aguirre (Miami) and Da’Karri Nelson (Penn 
State) could make big impacts. And the secondary adds Georgia CB 
Ondre Evans and Penn State safety King Mack (58 tackles, 3 passes 
defended) to go with second-year starting CB Brian Nelson. Even if they 
lose the opener at Virginia, which feels like a coin-flip game, Richmond, 
Appalachian State, Wake Forest, Stanford, Florida State and North 
Carolina all feel like wins. So we would need just two more wins from 
going to Virginia, at Vanderbilt, vs. Cal, vs. Duke and vs. Syracuse. That 
feels very doable.
ARKANSAS UNDER 4.5 WINS (-166)
Ryan Silverfield was a weird hire for Arkansas. It felt like he did less 
with more in the American Conference and was somehow rewarded. 
Well, congratulations, Ryan. You’re an SEC head coach, with possibly the 
fewest resources, and in your first year you have a top-five most difficult 
schedule. Week 2 at Utah is followed a week later by Georgia. Tulsa on 
September 26th feels like a win, but it’s a dreaded lookahead spot with 
a trip to Texas A&M looming the following week. They finish with a 
brutal run starting on Halloween with Missouri at home, at an improved 
Auburn squad, vs. South Carolina, at Texas and vs. LSU. I don’t see four 
wins, let alone five. It looks like, at best, wins are vs. North Alabama, 
Tulsa and maybe at Vanderbilt. Whichever QB the Razorbacks choose 
will lack experience. AJ Hill played in two games for Memphis last year, 
going 19 for 32, 223 passing yards, one TD and one INT. KJ Jackson saw 
action in five games for Arkansas, completing 33 of 54 passes for 441 
yards and three TDs. Expect this team to keep the ball on the ground 
with a deep stable of RBs: Braylen Russell is a bruiser, Sutton Smith ran 
for 669 yards and seven TDs at Memphis, and Jasper Parker was a four-
star recruit at Michigan. Former Boise five-star Chris Marshall went for 
30 catches, 574 yards and two TDs last season, but can they get 
him the ball consistently? They brought in some big transfers 
to fix a defense that was 129th in scoring a year ago, but this 
doesn’t seem like a team built to play from behind. And I expect 
them to be behind a lot this year with that schedule.
Braylen Russell

averaged 39 PPG, and with some small improvements this Air Force 
team will be flying high.

WES REYNOLDS
PENN STATE TO MAKE
COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF (+450)
Last year, Penn State had College Football Playoff and 
championship aspirations. Then, they lost in 2OT at home in 
the big showdown with Oregon, and that started a six-game losing streak, 
and James Franklin was fired after consecutive losses as over 20-point 
favorites at UCLA and vs. Northwestern. The Nittany Lions rallied under 
interim coach Terry Smith, still on staff as assistant head coach, to make 
and win a bowl game.
Enter Matt Campbell and 24 transfers (seven offensive starters and four 
defensive starters) from Iowa State. Call it Curt Cignetti and James Madison to 
Indiana from two years ago on steroids. Campbell led Cyclones football to its 
best decade in program history with seven bowl appearances in 10 seasons. 
All of college football wondered when he was going to make the leap to the 
bigger job, and he finally did when Penn State came calling. Campbell was 
not AD Pat Kraft’s first choice, but he may end up being the right choice.
The core of his Iowa State teams are now wearing dark blue and white in 
Happy Valley. Those teams went 17-7 over the last two seasons, including 
four victories over ranked teams, with QB Rocco Becht not missing a 
start in over three seasons despite playing through a variety of injuries. 
Shoulder surgery kept him out of spring practice except for 7-on-7.
Like Cignetti and the JMU crew from two years ago at Indiana, these 
players and coaches will have a chip on their shoulders to prove they can 
play against the step up in class against tougher competition. Also like that 
group, Penn State is the beneficiary of a highly favorable schedule. Out of 
their 12 games, the Nittany Lions are likely underdogs in only two of them, 
at Michigan and at Washington. They avoid all of the consensus top-three 
Big Ten teams in the regular season: Oregon, Ohio State, and Indiana.
While this is the first year for these Iowa State players in the Big Ten, 
they do have experience playing physical, grinder Big Ten games against 
Iowa in the CyHawk game, where the Cyclones defeated Kirk Ferentz 
and Iowa in three of the last four years.
If the College Football Playoff shakes out like last year, there will be four 
SEC teams, Notre Dame getting in this year, the Big 12 champion, the ACC 
champion, the Group of Six representative, and four Big Ten teams. The 
battle for the likely fourth Big Ten spot should be between Michigan, USC, 
and Penn State. Michigan and USC both have more difficult schedules.
Penn State, unlike last season, gets to also be the beneficiary of lower 
expectations.
We Are!
RUTGERS UNDER 5.5 WINS (-150)
Greg Schiano’s second act at Rutgers in the Big Ten has proven to be 
more difficult than his first act in the Big East. The NIL era has been 
even less kind to the Scarlet Knights, and player retention is certainly 
an issue, as Rutgers needs to make a decision to put more resources into 
the program if they are going to be competitive in the Big Ten.
Rutgers does have two All-Big Ten offensive skill players in RB Antwan 
Raymond and WR KJ Duff. However, they will have a new QB responsible 
for getting them the ball, as “The Greek Rifle” Athan Kaliakmanis has 
graduated. Boston College transfer Dylan Lonergan and returner AJ 
Surace are battling for the starting job. The Scarlet Knights are also 
looking for three new starters on the OL.
Defensively, though, is where Rutgers has been an absolute mess. The 
Scarlet Knights ranked 125th nationally in total defense, which is why 
Travis Johansen was brought in as defensive coordinator after coaching 
South Dakota to the FCS Playoffs last year.
While the non-conference slate is manageable (vs. UMass, at Boston College, 
vs. Howard), Rutgers is likely to be an underdog in every conference game 
except for perhaps the season finale against Michigan State.
Schiano’s teams always fight hard, but the talent, especially on defense, 
is still lacking.

2026 VSiN COLLEGE FOOTBALL BETTING GUIDE
Revenge is often an overrated angle, and Notre Dame coach Marcus Freeman is not playing it up. After the Fighting Irish got the cold shoulder from the 
College Football Playoff committee in December, Freeman didn’t complain or look for sympathy. He took accountability, essentially saying his team was 
left out because it left some doubt.
Notre Dame lost its first two games by a total of four points, but those were by far the most important games of its season. In the end, a 10-game win 
streak against a bunch of cupcakes and a couple of fringe ranked teams was not enough to overcome a slow start. That’s why “Leave No Doubt” is 
Freeman’s motto for the Irish this season.
While there is some revenge to exact against Miami, the Irish are focused on the bigger picture and will be playing the role of avengers — an angry 
group seeking to inflict punishment and setting out for retributive justice for the way last year’s team was wronged by the committee and the system.
Of course, Notre Dame is always polarizing, inspiring either love or hate with little middle ground, similar to In-N-Out Burger, LeBron James or a high-
ranking political figure. While some haters will say it was right to exclude the Irish from the playoff, the truth is it was wrong. Oddsmakers know it was 
wrong, and the power rankings showed it.
At the end of last season, Notre Dame was No. 3 in my power rankings, behind only Ohio State and Indiana. A flawed CFP system that included James 
Madison and Tulane also welcomed Southeastern Conference pretenders Oklahoma and Alabama into the 12-team bracket. There is no doubt the Irish 
would have been favored against all four of those teams.
On a neutral field in a playoff game, the Buckeyes might have been the only team favored against the Fighting Irish. How about the Hoosiers? Indiana, 
the 16-0 national champion, has not been defeated since it was a 7-point underdog in a 27-17 loss at Notre Dame in the first round of the 2024 playoff.
That’s a long setup for this announcement: Notre Dame is No. 1 in the VSiN preseason Top 50 for 2026. The decision is not unanimous and the numbers 
show it’s a close call. This poll is a result of power rankings created by me and professional handicapper Paul Stone. After the two sets of rankings 
produced an average number for each team, there were some ties. In this case, I broke the tie and ranked the Irish at the top with Oregon No. 2 and 
Ohio State No. 3.
“My top five are bunched tightly, but when in doubt, go with Ohio State,” said Stone, who ranks the Buckeyes first. “Is there a more complete team than 
Oregon on paper entering the season? I don’t think so. If someone wants to argue that Notre Dame should be the preseason No. 1, I’m not offering much 
resistance.”
“There isn’t much separating the top seven teams,” Fox Sports analyst Chris “The Bear” Fallica said. “One could throw Texas, Georgia, Ohio State, 
Oregon, Indiana, Miami and Notre Dame into a hat and pull them out in any order and I’d probably say, ‘OK, I can buy that.’”
Notre Dame will be favored in all 12 games and likely a double-digit favorite in 10 of those games. Sophomore quarterback CJ Carr, who debuted in a 
27-24 loss at Miami last year, is one of the Heisman Trophy favorites along with Texas quarterback Arch Manning.
“The Irish enter the season with the nation’s top defense, and few would be surprised if Carr leaves Manhattan with the Heisman the second Saturday in 
December,” Stone said.
Notre Dame also has a “kind schedule,” Stone noted, but the schedule is not a factor in my power rating. I favor the Irish over every other team on a 
neutral field, even if it’s by only one or two points against the other teams in the top five. Miami and BYU are the strongest opponents set to face the 
Irish, who open the season against Wisconsin at Lambeau Field.
If you start a power rating simply by grading the coach, quarterback and defense, who rates better than Notre Dame? The Irish return 10 starters on 
defense, Carr matured quickly as a freshman with 24 touchdown passes to six interceptions, and Freeman guided the Irish to the national title game 
after the 2024 season.
In his preview magazine, Phil Steele noted, “This defense is loaded with depth and talent at every level. All nine sets of my power ratings are calling for 
12-0. ND has playoff experience and a great shot at winning it all.”
It can be argued Oregon deserves to be No. 1, and the same goes for Ohio State. The Ducks, who return quarterback Dante Moore and much more, could 
be the fourth different Big Ten team in four years to win it all. The Buckeyes bring back quarterback Julian Sayin and wideout Jeremiah Smith, who has 
163 receptions for 2,558 yards and 27 touchdowns in two seasons, but they lost seven NFL draft picks on the defensive side.
“The Buckeyes have to replace some elite talent in the back two levels of their defense, but they have allowed less than 13 points a game in each of the past 
three seasons, and Jeremiah Smith is arguably the most impactful player in college football,” Stone said. “The Ducks are stacked on both lines and have no 
apparent weaknesses. One of these days (coach) Dan Lanning is going to break through and bring a championship to Eugene. Might this be the year?”
Fallica is hesitant to buy the Longhorns, who have reached the playoff two of the past 
three years and bring back Manning and dominant defensive end Colin Simmons, 
among many others. Everything is bigger with Texas, which is reportedly spending 
$35 million on its player roster and close to $25 million on its coaching staff.
“I think Texas is No. 1 heading into the season based solely on numbers, but factor 
in the schedule and they certainly could go 9-3,” Fallica said. “The Longhorns 
predictably did well in the transfer portal and Manning played at a much higher level 
over the second half of the season.”
The Longhorns went 7-1 to finish last season, with Georgia dealing the loss, 35-10. 
The Bulldogs are a popular pick to win the SEC with a stronger defense and veteran 
quarterback.
My power rankings, combined with Stone’s rankings, form the VSiN preseason Top 50.

2026 VSiN COLLEGE FOOTBALL BETTING GUIDE
1. NOTRE DAME
If sophomore quarterback CJ Carr stays healthy, the Irish should go 
12-0 and claim the top seed in the CFP. Two running backs were drafted 
in the NFL’s first round and both (Jeremiyah Love and Jadarian Price) 
were from Notre Dame, yet that position is still loaded with talent and 
features Aneyas Williams, Kedren Young and Nolan James. The offensive 
line ranks among the nation’s best, and Ohio State transfer Quincy 
Porter boosts the receiving corps. The defense is elite. This team is 
highly motivated and shows no weaknesses.
2. OREGON
Ducks coach Dan Lanning lost his defensive coordinator (Tosh Lupoi, 
California) and offensive coordinator (Will Stein, Kentucky) to head 
coaching jobs, but he doesn’t lose often. Lanning is 48-8 in four years, 
including 17-1 in Big Ten play the past two years. The downside is the 
Ducks were blown out by eventual national champions Ohio State and 
Indiana in playoff games the past two years. Senior quarterback Dante 
Moore will be an early NFL pick, and the defensive front is arguably the 
nation’s strongest.
3. OHIO STATE
The Buckeyes are as good as it gets at the offense’s most important 
positions with quarterback Julian Sayin (77% completions and 32 
touchdowns last season), running back Bo Jackson (1,090 yards) and 
receiver Jeremiah Smith (87 receptions, 1,243 yards and 12 touchdowns). 
The defense must replace a lot of NFL talent, though reloading is seldom 
a problem. The Michigan monkey, meaning a four-game losing streak, 
is finally off coach Ryan Day’s back, but now he’s got a Curt Cignetti 
problem and plays at Indiana in October.
4. GEORGIA
In the so-called ‘year of the quarterback’ in college football, Georgia 
senior Gunner Stockton is often overlooked because he’s not a top NFL 
prospect. But he’s a clutch dual-threat playmaker (24 passing and 10 
rushing touchdowns last season), and leading rusher Nate Frazier also 
returns. Two-time national championship coach Kirby Smart is 40-5 in 
SEC play since 2021. “Georgia’s offense might lack the firepower of some 
of the other contenders, but the Dawgs can run the ball and play sound 
defense,” Stone said.
5. TEXAS
Big checks were written to get Arch Manning more offensive help as 
coach Steve Sarkisian brought in Auburn receiver Cam Coleman and 
NC State running back Hollywood Smothers. Sark also made a sharp 
hire by getting Will Muschamp as defensive coordinator. “Manning 
rebounded nicely last season after stumbling through September,” Stone 
said. “Manning has the top trio of receivers (Coleman, Ryan Wingo 
and Emmett Mosley) in the country, plus his running ability will be 
showcased more this season.”
6. INDIANA
The Hoosiers were No. 16 in these power 
rankings a year ago, so are they underrated 
again? Curt Cignetti, 27-2 in two seasons in 
Bloomington, is a former Nick Saban assistant 
who looks like the new version of him. Top 
overall pick Fernando Mendoza and seven other 
draft picks are gone to the NFL. Cignetti sees 
something in TCU quarterback Josh Hoover (42 
turnovers in 31 career starts). Indiana ranked 
No. 2 in scoring defense (11.7 ppg) but will 
be near the top again despite losing some key 
players.
7. MIAMI
Cignetti got a few scares last season, and one 
came from the Hurricanes in a 27-21 national 
title game. Duke transfer quarterback Darian Mensah could be an 
upgrade from Carson Beck. Mensah benefits from the return of leading 
rusher Mark Fletcher (1,192 yards, 10 touchdowns) and leading receiver 
Malachi Toney (109 catches, 1,211 yards and 10 touchdowns). First-
round draft picks Rueben Bain and Akheem Mesidor will be missed on 
the defensive front. Miami has never won the ACC and coach Mario 
Cristobal’s team is the odds-on favorite (-135).
8. LSU
New coach Lane Kiffin used LSU’s resources to hit the transfer portal and 
the haul was huge. The top quarterbacks (Sam Leavitt, Arizona State; Husan 
Longstreet, USC) are transfers, and so are the three top receivers (Eugene 
Wilson, Florida; Jackson Harris, Hawaii; Winston Watkins, Ole Miss) and 
veteran left tackle Jordan Seaton (Colorado). Senior linebacker Whit Weeks 
and transfer end Princewill Umanmielen (Ole Miss) lead the defense.
9. MISSISSIPPI
Pete Golding won two of three playoff games after taking over for Kiffin, 
and his job as head coach was made much easier when dual-threat 
quarterback Trinidad Chambliss (4,464 total yards and 30 touchdowns) 
was granted an extra year of eligibility and running back Kewan Lacy 
(1,567 rushing yards, 24 TDs) returned. Golding lost two defensive 
starters to LSU, but the defense will be strong. The schedule is brutal, so 
Golding will be tested.
10. OKLAHOMA
Senior quarterback John Mateer had a hot hand to start last season, but 
he never was the same after a hand injury. Expectations are high for 
Mateer, who suddenly resembles a bodybuilder and should put up big 
numbers. Brent Venables is not a great head coach, but he can coach 
defense with the best of them, and the Sooners return senior safety 
Peyton Bowen and several other veterans from the nation’s No. 7 scoring 
defense (15.5 ppg).
11. TEXAS A&M
In two years in College Station, coach Mike Elko has won 19 games. His 
11-2 record last season was a bit of a downer considering the Aggies lost 
their final two games to Texas and Miami. Junior quarterback Marcel 
Reed can look electric at times, but he slumped and put up a total of only 
20 points in the losses to the Longhorns and Hurricanes. It’s not going to 
be easy for Elko to replace 10 players who were NFL picks.
12. TEXAS TECH
This news did not fly under the radar: quarterback Brendan Sorsby, 
a transfer from Cincinnati, departed the program amid a gambling 
controversy. Will Hammond is returning from a knee injury and should 
be fine as the starter when healthy. Red Raiders coach Joey McGuire had 
the money to reload after losing five defensive starters to the NFL. Texas 
Tech is the Big 12 favorite (-105) thanks to a ridiculously soft schedule.
13. BYU
The second choice on the Big 12 odds board is BYU (+550), but coach 
Kalani Sitake does not draw an easy schedule. Back-to-back games 
versus Notre Dame (Oct. 17) and at UCF (Oct. 24) will be pivotal. The 
Cougars are loaded with experience and talent on defense. The offense 
is in good hands with sophomore quarterback Bear Bachmeier (3,033 
passing yards and 15 touchdowns; 527 rushing yards and 11 TDs) and 
star running back LJ Martin.
15. ALABAMA
It was never going to be easy to follow Nick Saban, and Kalen DeBoer 
has made it look difficult. DeBoer is 20-8 in two seasons, which is OK at 
most programs but not in Tuscaloosa. Replacing first-round quarterback 
Ty Simpson will be either Keelon Russell or Austin Mack. There are all 
sorts of questions all over the offensive depth chart. There is plenty of 
talent on defense, but the Crimson Tide will enter the season as a boom-
or-bust mystery team.
14. USC
It’s time for Lincoln Riley to reach the CFP in his fifth year as 
USC coach. Two seniors — quarterback Jayden Maiava (3,711 
passing yards, 24 touchdowns) and running back Waymond 
Jordan — will operate behind one of the nation’s top offensive 
lines. The defensive line is also a strength. Riley pulled in a top-
ranked recruiting class and needs to win now. The Trojans host 
Ohio State, Oregon and Washington and play at Indiana, Penn 
State and Wisconsin.

16. WASHINGTON
The Demond Williams saga in January threatened to derail Washington’s 
season before it started. Williams entered the transfer portal for a better 
deal, but the dual-threat quarterback jumped the gun and basically 
was forced to return to Seattle. Williams totaled 3,676 yards and 31 
touchdowns. Third-year coach Jedd Fisch (9-4 last season) should carry 
playoff hopes into November, when the Huskies host Indiana and Penn 
State and finish at Oregon.
17. PENN STATE
Rocco Becht should feel at home in Happy Valley, and that’s because 
the senior quarterback will have more than 20 of his former Iowa State 
teammates with him. Matt Campbell took the Nittany Lions’ coaching 
and took a bunch of Cyclones, including leading rusher Carson Hansen, 
along for the ride. D’Anton Lynn, formerly at USC and UCLA, was a good 
hire as defensive coordinator. The schedule sets up well for Campbell to 
win at least eight games.
19. LOUISVILLE
A year after losing the quarterback competition at Ohio State, Lincoln 
Kienholz will probably help the Cardinals win a lot of games in the 
ACC. Jeff Brohm, who coached Purdue to the Big Ten title game in 
2022 and has a 28-12 record at Louisville, is an overachiever. Leading 
rusher Isaac Brown is back and an experienced offensive line looks 
outstanding. The Cardinals host SMU and Pitt and don’t play Miami 
and Clemson.
20. MICHIGAN
The hiring of Kyle Whittingham, who spent 21 years as Utah’s coach, 
was a home run even if he’s lost something off his fastball. He inherits a 
high-priced quarterback project in sophomore Bryce Underwood, who 
failed to develop under the previous staff. The backup QBs are promising 
if Underwood flops, and leading rusher Jordan Marshall returns. A big 
question mark shadows this Wolverines team, which Stone ranks 15th 
and I rank 28th.
21. IOWA
The Hawkeyes had Indiana on the ropes early last season and blew the 
game, 20-15, in Iowa City. Iowa also let one get away in an 18-16 loss to 
Oregon. Still, the Hawkeyes finished 9-4 with a bowl win as 28th-year 
coach Kirk Ferentz always seems to get to at least eight wins. He lost 
seven NFL draft picks and has to hope Hank Brown, last year’s backup 
quarterback, and running back Kamari Moulton can move the offense.
22. UTAH
Devon Dampier is a dynamic playmaker who passed for 24 touchdowns and 
rushed for 10 last season when the Utes went 11-2. Dampier and leading 
returning rusher Wayshawn Parker will help new coach Morgan Scalley keep 
up Utah’s high standards for winning. Scalley was the defensive coordinator 
for 10 years under Kyle Whittingham. The Utes do have some concerns on 
the offensive and defensive lines for the first time in a long time.
23. HOUSTON
It took only one year for coach Willie Fritz to turn around the Cougars, 
who went from 4-8 in his debut to 10-3 last season. Houston’s offense 
should be high-flying as veteran quarterback Conner Weigman (36 total 
touchdowns, including 25 through the air) comes back and is backed up 
by No. 1-ranked recruit Keisean Henderson. Top receiver Amare Thomas 
(12 TDs) returns. A defense full of veterans appears strong enough to 
survive in the Big 12.
24. CLEMSON
Change with the times or get left behind. Dabo Swinney is finally 
changing by hitting the transfer portal. He also changed offensive 
coordinators and brought back Chad Morris. Christopher Vizzina (and 
maybe freshman Tait Reynolds) replace longtime starting QB Cade 
Klubnik, who was drafted by the Jets. Senior end Will Heldt leads a 
defense that lost five NFL draft picks. Clemson hosts Miami on Oct. 3 
and could contend for the ACC title.
25. SMU
Senior quarterback Kevin Jennings has playoff experience from two 
years ago, and although he slipped some and turned the ball over too 
often last season, hopes are high for the offense (32.2 ppg) with the 
addition of Cal transfer running back Kendrick Raphael. The defense is 
being rebuilt. Rhett Lashlee has been a bet-on coach in ACC play  — the 
Mustangs upset Miami as 10-point underdogs last year — with a 38-16 
record in four years in Dallas.
26. TENNESSEE
Volunteers coach Josh Heupel finds ways 
to create offense and he needs to develop 
highly-touted freshman quarterback Faizon 
Brandon in a hurry. It will help to have 
leading rusher DeSean Bishop (1,076 yards, 
16 touchdowns) in the backfield again. New 
defensive coordinator Jim Knowles, formerly 
at Penn State and Ohio State, will make a 
difference.
27. MISSOURI
The Tigers started 5-0 last season and 
won eight regular-season games prior to a 
disappointing bowl performance. Ahmad 
Hardy (1,649 yards and 16 touchdowns) is the catalyst for the offense 
and arguably the best running back in the SEC. Ole Miss transfer Austin 
Simmons is the new quarterback. One problem is a new-look defense 
that won’t be improved.
28. ARIZONA
With 72 touchdown passes as a three-year starter in Tucson, Noah Fifita 
is one of the Big 12’s best and he gives the Wildcats a shot in almost every 
game. Arizona (9-4) lost three games by six points or fewer last season. 
The Wildcats will get tough tests on the road in September (BYU), 
October (Texas Tech) and November (Kansas State).
29. VIRGINIA TECH
One team’s trash is another team’s treasure. Penn State fans are happy 
to get rid of coach James Franklin after 12 years and Virginia Tech fans 
are thrilled to have him. The Hokies (3-9) will be much improved due to 
Franklin’s ability to recruit talent. “Big Game” James gets a soft launch 
with the toughest road games (Clemson, SMU and Miami) late in the 
season.
30. SOUTH CAROLINA
Overhyped as a top NFL prospect a year ago, quarterback LaNorris 
Sellers slumped as a passer as the Gamecocks slipped from 9-4 to 4-8. 
Sellers totaled 25 touchdowns in 2024 and that number dipped to 18 last 
season. Are you buying or selling? Shane Beamer is coaching a more 
experienced team, but the schedule is brutal and there are concerns in 
Columbia.
31. MINNESOTA
P.J. Fleck is money in bowl games (7-0) as coach of the Golden Gophers, 
and he’s consistent with 8-5 records each of the past two years. He’s got 
a good shot to be a winner again with quarterback Drake Lindsey and 
leading rusher Darius Taylor returning. Senior end Anthony Smith is 
one of the Big Ten’s best defensive players.
32. KANSAS STATE
Bill Snyder, one of the all-time greats, and Chris Klieman, who retired in 
December, are extremely tough coaching acts to follow at K-State. Collin 
Klein, a former Wildcats quarterback and offensive coordinator, takes 
over the top job. Veteran quarterback Avery Johnson and leading rusher 
Joe Jackson return, but multiple holes must be filled on defense.
18. FLORIDA
Jon Sumrall arrives from Tulane as the new coach and should 
be a breath of fresh air in Gainesville after fans suffered through 
the ill-fated “Sun Belt” Billy Napier era. Whether the Gators 
finish in the top half of the SEC will depend on who wins the 
QB job (Georgia Tech transfer Aaron Philo or last year’s backup, 
Tramell Jones) and how well he plays. Leading rusher Jadan 
Baugh (1,170 yards) returns, and the defense should be solid.

34. VIRGINIA
The Cavaliers cashed in on close-game luck last season by going 3-0 
in overtime games and winning another by two points, so don’t count 
on another 11-win season for coach Tony Elliott. Virginia has two new 
quarterbacks, Beau Pribula (Missouri) and Eli Holstein (Pitt). This 
team looks weaker, but a soft schedule excludes Miami, Clemson and 
Louisville.
35. AUBURN
New coach Alex Golesh, who won 23 games in three years at South 
Florida, has an offensive background and brought senior quarterback 
Byrum Brown with him. While leading rusher Jeremiah Cobb 
comes back, the entire receiving corps is new and includes two USF 
transfers. Junior linebacker Xavier Atkins (team-high 84 tackles, nine 
sacks) leads an inexperienced defense. The Tigers finished 1-7 in SEC 
play last year.
36. BOISE STATE
The Broncos (9-5 last season) won the last three Mountain West 
championships and are +170 favorites to win the eight-team Pac-12. If 
they don’t win the league, a defensive decline will likely be the reason. 
Boise could boast the conference’s top quarterback, Maddux Madsen, 
and top running back, Dylan Riley. Madsen must bounce back after 
regressing last season.
37. GEORGIA TECH
Dual-threat quarterback Haynes King led the Yellow Jackets to nine 
wins and put a scare into Georgia, but he’s gone and replaced by Alberto 
Mendoza. The brother of Heisman Trophy winner Fernando Mendoza 
transferred from Indiana, and running back Justice Haynes transferred 
from Michigan. The defense looks strong. Brent Key has been a bet-on 
coach as an underdog (15-5 ATS).
38. NEBRASKA
UNLV transfer quarterback Anthony Colandrea is the key to coach 
Matt Rhule’s success in his fourth season with the Cornhuskers. 
Colandrea totaled 4,080 yards (3,459 passing and 621 rushing) and 
32 touchdowns for the Rebels. Nebraska (7-6 last season) faces Ohio 
State, Oregon and Indiana but should have enough talent to go 
bowling again.
39. NORTH CAROLINA STATE
Junior quarterback CJ Bailey had offers if he hit the transfer portal, but 
the 6-6, 210-pounder stayed with the Wolfpack. Bailey passed for 3,105 
yards and 25 touchdowns while adding six rushing scores during an 
8-5 season. Leading rusher Hollywood Smothers transferred to Texas, 
but No. 2 rusher Jayden “Duke” Scott is back. Miami is not on the ACC 
schedule.
40. VANDERBILT
Adjusting to life after quarterback Diego Pavia, a Heisman finalist, 
won’t be easy, but the Commodores won’t be bad. Jared Curtis, the 
No. 2-ranked incoming freshman QB, can lean on a pair of seniors 
— running back Sedrick Alexander and wideout Junior Sherrill. 
Vandy coach Clark Lea (10-3 last season) will field another solid 
defense.
41. ARIZONA STATE
Kenny Dillingham has done an amazing 
coaching job at Arizona State. He followed 
a 3-9 debut season with records of 11-3 and 
8-5. His fourth season will probably fall 
somewhere in the middle as in 6-6. With 
quarterback Sam Leavitt transferring to LSU, 
the Sun Devils turn to Kentucky transfer 
Cutter Boley. The defense lost nine starters.
42. PITTSBURGH
As a freshman, Mason Heintschel passed for 
16 touchdowns and showed some running 
ability in his nine starts. Don’t expect to see 
a “Heintschel for Heisman” campaign, but 
he’s got potential and is supported by a veteran offensive line. Panthers 
coach Pat Narduzzi, who’s no game-management genius, will put 
together a decent defense.
43. ILLINOIS
Senior quarterback Katin Houser, a transfer from East Carolina, replaces 
Luke Altmyer in coach Bret Bielema’s run-oriented offense. The top three 
running backs return, but the offensive line is mostly new and won’t be 
improved. It’s a rebuilding year for the Fighting Illini defense. Bielema’s 
team will take steps back after going 9-4 and 10-3 the past two seasons.
44. CALIFORNIA
Tosh Lupoi, the former Oregon defensive coordinator, takes over in 
Berkeley. The Golden Bears lost most of their best defensive players and 
will rely on their offense to lead the way. Sophomore quarterback Jaron-
Keawe Sagapolutele seems to be a rising star after passing for 3,454 yards 
and 18 touchdowns for a 7-6 team.
45. NORTHWESTERN
A 19-19 record does not reflect how well David Braun has coached up the 
Wildcats in his three years. Braun inherited a seemingly hopeless 1-11 team. 
Northwestern’s strength should be its defense, although the coaching staff is 
intriguing with Chip Kelly taking over as offensive coordinator. The new QB 
is likely to be Michigan State transfer Aidan Chiles.
46. OKLAHOMA STATE
Mike Gundy is out after two decades, and new coach Eric Morris brings 
a big offensive reputation with him from North Texas. He’s also bringing 
quarterback Drew Mestemaker, who led the nation in passing yards 
(4,379) last year. The Cowboys (1-11 last season) could be the nation’s 
most improved team.
47. UCLA
The Bruins were bad last season at 3-9, but they did upset Penn State 
42-37 as 24-point underdogs in Pasadena. Bob Chesney, who coached 
James Madison to the CFP, is rebuilding with several transfers and will 
energize the program. Will he be able to rejuvenate inconsistent young 
quarterback Nico Iamaleava?
48. WISCONSIN
There was a lot of excitement in Madison when Luke Fickell was hired 
as coach in 2023, but the thrill is long gone after back-to-back losing 
seasons. The Badgers’ quarterback play was abysmal a year ago, and that 
should change with the addition of dual-threat Old Dominion transfer 
Colton Joseph. Wisconsin’s schedule ranks as the Big Ten’s easiest.
49. BAYLOR
After everything fell apart at Florida, young quarterback DJ Lagway 
transferred to Baylor. Lagway, once hyped as one of the nation’s top 
recruits, can be electric if he’s playing with confidence. He’s replacing 
Sawyer Robertson, who passed for 31 touchdowns last season. Bears 
coach Dave Aranda must improve the defense and win or he’s done in 
Waco.
50. NAVY
After an 11-2 season, with the losses to Notre Dame and North Texas, 
the Midshipmen must replace star quarterback Blake Horvath. Braxton 
Woodson, who’s 6-3 and 215 pounds, will have big shoes to fill. Navy has 
a physical offensive line and a solid defense, but the key to the season 
will be Woodson, who’s fast and skilled but has not played much.
33. TCU
After Indiana swooped in to swipe quarterback Josh Hoover, 
the Horned Frogs looked to the Ivy League for an answer. 
Jaden Craig, a first team all-conference passer at Harvard, will 
run coach Sonny Dykes’ offense. Since getting crushed 65-7 
by Georgia in the 2022 national championship game, TCU 
has posted records of 5-7, 9-4 and 9-4. Dykes destroyed Bill 
Belichick and North Carolina 48-14 in last season’s opener. The 
rematch is in Ireland.

2026 VSiN COLLEGE FOOTBALL BETTING GUIDE
The college football landscape is changing 
literally and figuratively this season, as 
the Pac-12 is back with eight teams, the 
Mountain West looks a lot different, and a 
team from California will play in the MAC. 
Home-field advantage is probably more 
dynamic than ever, in the sense that it 
depends on a variety of factors. Having one 
simple baseline probably isn’t enough, but 
having something is better than nothing 
and that has been my approach over the last 
several seasons.
Playing at home is never really going to 
be a bad thing, so there is still an inherent 
“advantage”, even though its value will 
always be subjective. Weather, rest, travel, 
and all of the usual factors come into play, 
but there are others. A night game in Death 
Valley (either one) is going to carry more 
weight than a noon kickoff against a Group 
of Six school. A school where the basketball 
program outpaces the football program could see home-field lessened once 
November rolls around and students are more invested in hoops. How invested 
are the alums and adults in that particular program nowadays? It’s very hard to 
pin down these qualitative factors.
But, at least if we have some kind of value in mind, we can adjust accordingly, 
whether we actually attempt to quantify all of those variables or just keep them 
in mind when handicapping the game. To find that baseline, I’ve decided to take 
a three-year sample of home records, as that would seem to capture the team’s 
current state and also create a sample size large enough to minimize some noise. 
With over 100 different head coaches and thousands of transfers in FBS over 
the last three seasons, even three years may be tricky, but it seems like a happy 
medium.
Based on the straight up (SU) and against the spread (ATS) home win percentages 
for these teams, I’ve created a series of buckets. The standard home-field 
advantage I’ve settled on is two points. For teams that sit between 40% and 
59.99% at home, their home-field advantage is two points. For teams above or 
below those thresholds, the HFA varies.
For this season, there are 24 teams with my max HFA of 3.5 points for having a 
SU + ATS Win% of 70% or higher. There are 16 teams with 3 points of HFA for 
a SU + ATS Win% of 65-69.99%. There are 24 teams with 2.5 points of HFA for 
60-64.99%.
On the flip side, there are eight teams with 1.5 points of HFA for 35.01-39.99% 
and eight teams with 1 point of HFA for 35% or lower. Again, I want to stress 
that I consider these numbers to be starting points for creating point spreads on 
games. All of those factors and variables mentioned above should be considered 
on a case-by-case basis.
The home records are courtesy of Steve Makinen and his extensive 
database, so my thanks go out to our VSiN Analytics Guru.
Here are those teams for the 2026 season.
With the HFA numbers established for all 138 FBS teams, those are then put 
together with my college football power ratings to produce a game spread. If 
my power ratings have Ohio State 14 points better than USC and the game is in 
Columbus, that would make my line on the game Buckeyes -17.5 with their 3.5 
points of home-field advantage.
This season, I expect to have some deviations on a week-to-week basis in 
conference play, since we have Sacramento State in the MAC, Northern Illinois 
in the Mountain West, and Texas State in the Pac-12, just as some examples 
of conference realignment and how those teams will be visiting new venues, 
playing at elevation, or having long travel with some odd kickoff times. Similarly, 
teams that go to them will be doing something different.
As I continue to say, home-field advantage is an “inexact science”, but a true case 
of ‘something is better than nothing’ and at least there is some sort of criteria that 
teams meet in order to have the values that they do.

2026
college football win 
totals I’m betting 
now
After going back through the coaching changes, the Stability Scores, 
the transitional systems, the recruiting rankings, and playing out the 
schedule by my power ratings, I’ve locked in on my team season-win 
total bets that I will be making. You’ll see that based upon the recent 
success I’ve enjoyed, I’ve again opted for more Unders than Overs this 
season.
 
My overall four-year record is now 57-42-2 for 57.6%, highlighted by 34-
17-1 (66.7%) on Unders. I have become much better at identifying teams 
that are due for struggles. Hopefully I can see a clearer picture of which 
teams will improve this year.
14 teams I project to go Over their 
DraftKings season win props
 
BOISE STATE – OVER 7.5 WINS
The Broncos +1.7 difference represents one of the biggest I’ve ever had in 
projecting wins against the schedule using my power ratings, and I even 
double- and triple-checked the numbers to be sure. I think the oddsmakers 
are giving a bit too much credit to the strength of the new Pac-12, and in 
my opinion, BSU is the obvious favorite. QB Maddux Madsen returns as 
a senior, and head coach Spencer Danielson is in his fourth year with the 
program. With the opener at Oregon the only likely loss I see on the 2026 
slate, I think Boise takes the newly formed Pac-12 and exceeds the modest 
win total of 7.5. I’d probably even be willing to bet it up to at least 8.5.
 
FRESNO STATE – OVER 6.5 WINS
Fresno State surprised me last season by exceeding expectations in 
head coach Matt Entz’s first year. Sometimes it takes a coach a bit of 
time to find his footing. In terms of FSU football, Entz did not, as his 
team finished 9-4. He responded to that success by adding an extremely 
improved recruiting class as graded by 247Sports. Considering the 
Bulldogs’ success last year, and now transitioning into the remade Pac-

group that didn’t drop off was a winning percentage bump of 15% (+3.2

FLORIDA ATLANTIC – OVER 5.5 WINS
Second-year head coach Zach Kittley’s first team at Florida Atlantic 
was, if nothing else, fun to watch. The Owls had the most offensive

game. Of those teams, only four regressed in the follow-up campaign,

at least four starters more than the prior season, only 40 got worse. The 
average improvement of the group that didn’t drop off was a winning 
percentage bump of 15% (+3.2 wins) and ATS rise of 6.7%. With a lot of

the chance to be FAU’s best football year since the Lane Kiffin days.
 
HOUSTON - OVER 8.5 WINS

141 teams over the last five years that brought back at least four starters

ILLINOIS – OVER 7.5 WINS

KANSAS STATE – OVER 7.5 WINS
It came as a bit of a shock for KSU fans when Chris Klieman announced 
his retirement as head football coach in December. He stepped away 
citing personal health and family considerations and did it with the 
Wildcats coming off a 6-6 season, but also with a reasonable amount 
of starting experience coming back. Leading that charge is third-year 
starting QB Avery Johnson. In Klieman’s place steps Collin Klein, 
who gets his first head coaching gig after spending seven seasons in 
Manhattan as an offensive assistant before serving as Texas A&M’s OC 
the last two years. As I look at last season, KSU was so close to bigger 
successes, but suffered five of its six losses by six points or fewer. That, 
combined with Johnson returning as a senior, makes this an ideal 
situation for Klein to step in and have some immediate positive impact. 
He played at KSU from 2008-12 so already has a tremendous bond with 
the program, and his hiring was met with a lot of optimism. With no 
Texas Tech or BYU on the 2026 slate, I think this team has an outside 
shot at contending for a Big 12 title game berth.
 
SOUTH ALABAMA – OVER 5.5 WINS
Sometimes, there’s no rhyme or reason to figuring out why a specific 
improvement or decline in a recruiting season occurs. I don’t think South 
Alabama fans care about the how or why here, but in his third season, 
coming off a disappointing 4-8 record, head coach Major Applewhite 
was able to secure his best recruit/transfer class this spring, with the 
86th ranking beating last year’s grade by 31 positions. Several of the 
newcomers are P4 transfers. It gives USA at least a shot at getting a lot 
better on the field this fall. Also encouraging is the fact that QB Bishop 
Davenport is back for his senior season after leading this team to 26.5 PPG 
last year. The Sun Belt Conference doesn’t have a lot of teams contending 
for the role of favorite this season, and the Jaguars’ conference slate is 
mild at best. I like this team to return to a bowl game this fall.
 
SOUTH CAROLINA – OVER 6.5 WINS
South Carolina dropped by five wins in the regular season last year, and 
quite honestly, it was unexpected. The Gamecocks lost four games by 
10 points or less, all against teams that were ranked in the Top 25 at the 
time. Fortunately for head coach Shane Beamer, many of the key players 
decided to steady the ship and come back for another run, including 
QB LaNorris Sellers, this team’s offensive star. This is another team with 
several key transition systems to consider, among them: 1) One of the 
biggest improvements in wins from one season to the next you’ll find 
comes when nine or more offensive starters, including the quarterback, 
return from a team that won 50% or less of its games outright in the 
prior season. The average win increase is +2.7 wins & 13.3% SU. 2) 
There have been 43 teams over the last five seasons that have endured 
losing seasons despite outscoring their opponents. Of those, 17 of them 
brought back 13 or more starters, including their quarterback. The 
collective improvement of this group of teams was about 20% SU (+3.4 
wins) and 8.9% ATS. These teams combined to go 56.5% ATS, a profit-
making collection. Beamer’s team has a realistic shot of heading to 
Florida in October with a 4-1 record at least. A win there would give this 
team a ton of momentum in returning to where they were two years ago.
 
SYRACUSE – OVER 4.5 WINS
There are a lot of reasons why teams can yo-yo from one season to the next 
nowadays in college football. Losing a lot of key players from a successful 
team the prior year is at the head of the list in terms of why teams might 
drop. That clearly affected Syracuse in 2025, as the Orange went from 
10-3 to 3-9. Turnovers can also be big, and they were for ‘Cuse last season. 
However, in the “there’s nowhere to go but up” category, since 2021, 
there have been 21 teams that have won four or fewer games in a season 
while enduring a -0.8 or worse turnover ratio. Only two of those 21 teams 
regressed. The average win improvement for the other 19 teams was 2.3 
per season, and the SU win % upgrade was 15.3%. Overall, recruiting at 
Syracuse has seen an upgrade under Fran Brown, who begins his third 
season with the program. He is obviously a pretty strong salesman, as 
he was able to land the second-highest-rated class the Orange have seen 
in the last 17 years, despite coming off a 3-9 record. With QB Steve Angeli 
back for his senior season, and the ACC looking down for 2026, I think the 
Orange have a good chance to rebound.
 
TEXAS – OVER 9.5 WINS
The pressure on Texas and QB Arch Manning last year was palpable; you 
could sense it every time they took the field. Expectations were beyond 
reasonable control. The fact that the Longhorns still won 10 games despite 
a 5-7-1 ATS record shows just how much even the experts behind the 
bookmaking counter thought of this group. Well, they say that all is well 
that ends well, and head coach Steve Sarkisian’s team won its final three

The offense put up 456 yards in the bowl win over Michigan. That is the 
momentum they will be carrying into 2026. In addition, a program that 
achieved its first-ever No. 1 recruiting ranking in the country on record 
last year, then followed it up with a No. 3 rank, seems due for lofty goals. 
There is one key transitional system I have my eye on regarding Texas: 
Only three of the last 33 teams since 2021 that had nine or more offensive 
returning starters, including the quarterback, from a team that won 45% 
or less of its games against the spread in the prior season, got worse. The 
average win increase of the other 30 teams was +2.0 wins, 6.7% SU, and 
16.8% ATS. These teams were also about 53% ATS. Two additional wins 
would put this team at 11-1. I think that’s realistic with the talent that is in 
place here and a QB 100% ready to fulfill his immense promise.

IOWA STATE – UNDER 5.5 WINS

KENTUCKY – UNDER 4.5 WINS
For Mark Stoops to last a decade in the SEC at perhaps the conference’s 
premier basketball school says a lot about the stability he brought to the 
Kentucky program. In all, he took the Wildcats to eight bowl games and 
won 82 games. His dismissal came after an embarrassing 41-0 season-
ending loss to Louisville, as university brass decided it was time to move 
on. The new hire is a Louisville guy, as Will Stein played quarterback 
there for five years and started his coaching career there some 13 years 
ago. Since then, he has made a few stops, including most recently 
serving as offensive coordinator for Oregon. He led a high-powered 
offense there with QB Dante Moore, but there isn’t that type of talent 
right now at UK, nor has there been on that side of the ball for a long

LIBERTY – UNDER 8.5 WINS
To this day, I’ve always been puzzled as to why head coach Jamey

MEMPHIS – UNDER 7.5 WINS
Charles Huff is making his third coaching stop in as many years after 
guiding Marshall and Southern Miss to successful seasons in 2024 and 
2025. He makes a jump up this time to Memphis, where he takes over a 
program that has been one of the better and most consistent Group of 
Five teams for the last decade-plus. Like his predecessors at Memphis,

teams got better the next season, and collectively, they dropped by an 
average of 17.2%, or 2.8 wins per season, as well as 11.4% ATS. As a

MISSOURI STATE – UNDER 4.5 WINS
It was a solid first season at the FBS level and in Conference USA for

a game they would eventually lose to Arkansas State. Year 2 at college 
football’s top level looks to be a little more challenging, however, as the 
program moves on from Ryan Beard, the head coach of the last three

NEBRASKA – UNDER 6.5 WINS

OHIO U – UNDER 6.5 WINS
Ohio U is another team undergoing massive change for first-year 
head coach John Hauser, although he was the DC here previously, so 
perhaps less change than other teams on this Under list. However, 
teams that are off of seasons in which they won 60% or more of their 
games outright and have four or fewer offensive starters returning, 
plus are breaking in a new quarterback, have dropped by an average 
of -3.7 wins, -26% outright, -11.7% ATS, and -6.6 PPG offensively. The 
eight teams that added a new head coach plummeted by 29% and 
-4.4 wins per season. A 4.4-win drop would put the Bobcats at 3.6-8.4. 
Now, while that may be a bit drastic considering the consistency this 
program has performed with over the last decade, a drop is expected 
nonetheless. I think we also need to consider that this team won five of 
its nine games by seven points or fewer. Radical change can turn that 
around quickly. Close wins are often characterized as getting “lucky” 
over the course of a season. Well, teams that have a lot of them and 
then come back inexperienced are naturally expected to drop. Over the 
last 13 seasons, 73 teams brought back 14 starters or fewer and had a 
new QB from a team that was fortunate to get four or more close wins 
of seven points or fewer in the prior season. Only 11 of these teams 
finished better the next season, with the average win drop being 2.6 
per season, a 16.7% plunge.
 
SACRAMENTO STATE – UNDER 4.5 WINS
In my opinion, there are even varied levels of Stability Scores of 
zero in college football nowadays. I don’t give negative numbers, 
but if I did, what Sacramento State and new head coach Alonzo 
Carter are facing in 2026 would qualify. Not only is he a new coach 
with a new staff and an almost entirely new roster, but his program 
is jumping from FCS to FBS and is playing in a conference in a 
completely different area of the country. And, here’s a weird one 
for you. As Sacramento State got ready for its final season of FCS-
level football a year ago, it scored a program-high 73rd-ranked 
incoming recruit/transfer class. As it transitions to FBS this year, 
the class is ranked 122nd. Perhaps potential recruits didn’t like the 
potential challenges of dealing with a MAC schedule, the Midwest, 
the mid-week games, etc. As one of the more consistent and high-
performing teams from the FCS, the Hornets believe they are 
ready to compete at the FBS level and in the MAC. The Hornets 
have won 7+ games in five of the last six seasons of football. 
That said, there have been 33 teams over the last six 
seasons that have recorded 4+ blowout wins of 20 
points or more one season, then had to change 
head coaches for one reason or another. Only 
five of the 33 teams got better the next 
season, and collectively, they dropped by 
an average of 17.2%, or 2.8 wins per 
season, as well as 11.4% ATS. As 
a group, they were 44.2% ATS. 
Phil Steele picks them last in 
the conference, behind 
even UMass, whose 
win total is 2.5. Yes, 
expectations are 
low.

UNDER 4.5 WINS
Recruiting efforts have dropped off

SOUTH FLORIDA – UNDER 8.5 WINS
I am as excited as anyone to see what Brian Hartline can do at South

-11.7% ATS, and -6.6 PPG offensively. The eight teams that added a new

TOLEDO – UNDER 7.5 WINS
There are 10 teams this season starting with Stability Scores of zero. One 
of them is Toledo, who, for the last decade or so, has annually been one 
of the more stable situations year-in and year-out. The Rockets program 
has been known for having a lot of returning starters each summer, and 
correspondingly, a lot of success under previous coach Jason Candle. 
Well, the first domino fell in the spring after Candle’s departure, as the

coaching staffs. Still, they are picked first in the conference by many

slight decline. I think this prop goes Under.

2026 VSiN COLLEGE FOOTBALL BETTING GUIDE
As much as college football has changed, some things still remain the same. Group of Five programs continue to provide a feeder 
system for the deeper-pocketed Power Four schools in terms of coaching staffs. The G5 - now G6 with the return of the Pac-12 - 
presently doubles as a minor league system of sorts in the NIL era, where players are hoping to get called up to a major conference and 
a significant payday. There used to be a big imbalance, where mostly coaches would preach brotherhood, family, and loyalty and then 
bounce to collect a bigger bag. Players have that opportunity now, too.
There are 138 FBS schools this season, and 35 of them (25.4%) have new head coaches, if we include guys who are interims or had 
the interim tag removed. While not quite the 31.3% in the NFL with 10 new sideline bosses for 32 teams, it is another year of drastic 
turnover with coaches and players in college football. Hitting the playbooks is becoming more difficult than hitting the textbooks, as 
some of these players will go through multiple coordinators and head coaches while they’re in school.
With 30 and 28 head coaching changes over the last two seasons, respectively, we’ve seen some teams gel very quickly and others 
struggle to have everything come together. These are not professionals; they are student-athletes. While most of them are paid to play, 
maturity levels vary wildly at this age and some schemes require more focus and learning than others. It is important to know the 
teams with the new head coaches for a variety of reasons, so let’s look at them and try to pinpoint some teams that could improve right 
away, improve gradually, or could be in for a rough year.
by Adam Burke

2026 VSiN COLLEGE FOOTBALL BETTING GUIDE
Charles Huff  Memphis
This will be an interesting season for Huff. He seemed like a bit of an odd hire at Marshall, having primarily served as 
a running backs coach in his career, but he was on Nick Saban’s staff when the Thundering Herd came calling. After a 
32-20 run in Huntington, he went to Southern Miss because Marshall let the reigning Sun Belt Conference champion 
head coach walk away. He took a big chunk of his roster to Southern Miss and went 7-5 before leveling up to Memphis. 
As mentioned above with Silverfield, Memphis has a pretty robust NIL budget thanks to FedEx and Huff, who has 
connections all over the country from his different stops, could find immediate and prolonged success with resources he 
didn’t have at his two previous stops.
Neal Brown  North Texas
I wouldn’t call myself a glass-half-full person by nature, but when it comes to new coaching hires, I’m often optimistic. I 
can’t say that about North Texas’s hire of Brown, who was let go from West Virginia in 2024 and served as Steve Sarkisian’s 
assistant in 2025. Brown has over 120 games of head coaching experience under his belt, all at the FBS level. He was very 
successful at Troy with three 10-win seasons in a row before heading to Morgantown. He is an offensive-minded guy, 
but not like Eric Morris, who ran more of a run-and-shoot style. It might work and the bar isn’t terribly high, given that 
the program has three winning seasons since 2013, but it feels like UNT is drifting closer to mediocrity again rather than 
living up to what should be their new standard.
Will Hall  Tulane
Losing Willie Fritz and then Jon Sumrall would be tough for any program, but not taking a third swing at a rising name 
feels like a miss. Instead, Tulane promoted pass game coordinator Will Hall, who had a miserable tenure at Southern 
Miss, going 14-30 over three seasons and seven games. Hall went to Hattiesburg after serving as Tulane’s OC in 2019-20 
and was a fairly hot commodity after some strong seasons at West Alabama and West Georgia as a young head coach, but 
his star faded after the Southern Miss years. It just feels like the Green Wave took the easy route and that seems really 
disappointing.
Brian Hartline  USF
Suffice it to say that December 3 was a day that Ohio State fans had been dreading for a long time. Hartline, who was a 
star WR for the Buckeyes from 2005-08, was on the staff in Columbus from 2017-25 and directly responsible for Marvin 
Harrison Jr., Garrett Wilson, Emeka Egbuka, Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Chris Olave, Carnell Tate, and now Jeremiah Smith. The 
absurd receiver pipeline is just one attractive element to Hartline, who was Ohio State’s OC/co-OC the last three seasons. 
USF is looking to keep up the offensive prowess they had under another Ohio State alum in Alex Golesh, but it’s fair to 
question Hartline’s experience outside of his offensive bubble. Just as important as Hartline might be DC Josh Aldridge, 
who is just in his second year calling plays.
AMERICAN

2026 VSiN COLLEGE FOOTBALL BETTING GUIDE
Tosh Lupoi  California
Lupoi’s first crack at being a head coach is with his alma mater and allows his coaching career to come full circle. Lupoi 
was a Golden Bear from 2000-05 and the program’s defensive line coach from 2008-11. In looking at Lupoi, it got me 
thinking about racehorses and bloodlines. Lupoi’s college coaching career has been under Jeff Tedford, Steve Sarkisian, 
Nick Saban, and Dan Lanning. He also spent three seasons in the NFL under Freddie Kitchens, Dan Quinn, and Urban 
Meyer. There is a ton of coaching experience in that list and the 44-year-old Lupoi had to pick up a lot of things. On the 
other hand, even well-bred horses don’t always work out and Lupoi, who follows another guy who had a lot of good 
mentors in Justin Wilcox, is another defensive-minded guy at a place that badly needs an injection of offense. 
Tavita Pritchard  Stanford
In retrospect, I don’t think we give enough credit to Jim Harbaugh and David Shaw for what they did at Stanford. If 
somebody can replicate that in today’s NIL era, it will be one of the best coaching jobs we’ve ever seen. The program got a 
$50 million donation in October 2025 from former player Bradford Freeman and had instituted a revenue-sharing model 
in the spring of 2025. Even with the weight that a Stanford degree carries, Andrew Luck, and now Pritchard, who played 
for the Cardinal from 2006-09 and coached for them from 2011-22, know the academic requirements in Palo Alto severely 
limit the player pool. Pritchard has spent the last three seasons with the Commanders coaching up QBs, including, of 
course, Jayden Daniels. “Unimaginative” is the best way to describe the hire after Frank Reich responded to Luck’s plea to 
serve as a stopgap last season.
James Franklin  Virginia Tech
I made sure to double-check that Ohio State and Michigan did not move to the ACC before discussing Franklin. The guy 
is a solid motivator, a good recruiter, and a pretty lackluster in-game coach, but the conference lacks premier teams right 
now, and this is a perfect landing spot for him. As a guy who is just 8-7 in bowl games and 2-1 in the CFP, he’s had a very 
high regular-season floor with two 9-4 seasons at Vanderbilt in the early 2010s when that was a rough job, and six double-
digit winning seasons at Penn State. There’s a lot of talent in the Hokies’ pipeline and Franklin, a southeastern PA native, 
should do very well recruiting in the DMV and the Keystone State. This could be and should be a quick transformation.
ACC
James Franklin
